- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.7) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 5–10 days.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ 0.3) or shows sharp decline, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 3–7% for next 7–14 days.  
- After a price spike (forecast > 72), model frequently overcorrects downward; cap downward correction at 10% of spike magnitude.  
- If 3+ consecutive forecast days are above 70, model often fails to account for mean reversion; apply downward bias of 1–3% per day until price stabilizes.  
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently overestimates early in the forecast window (first 5–7 days); apply 1–3% downward adjustment to first 5 days.  
- If sentiment history shows volatility (alternating +/– values), model tends to overfit short-term noise; smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 values before final output.
